subject: zoology
question_text: A person is suffering from bowel irregularity, abdominal pain, blood and mucus in stool, etc. Based on these symptoms, name the disease and its causative organism.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.58, VSAQ 135). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Disease
lines: The symptoms given are those of amoebic
steps.why: Blood and mucus together in the stool point to ulcers in the wall of the large intestine, and that is what separates amoebic dysentery from ordinary loose motions.
common_mistakes: Answering 'diarrhoea'. Blood and mucus in the stool make it dysentery.
Answering malaria or ascariasis. Those do not give blood and mucus in the stool.
steps.memory_tip: Blood and mucus in the stool means ulcers in the large intestine, and that means amoebic dysentery.
steps.margin_note: One line. Give both names of the disease if you can.

steps.label: Causative organism
lines: The disease is caused by Entamoeba histolytica,
which lives in the large intestine of man.
Its trophozoites make ulcers in the intestinal
wall, and the ulcers ooze blood and mucus.
steps.why: Naming the organism is only half the mark here; the link between its trophozoites and the ulcers is what explains the symptoms in the question.
common_mistakes: Writing only 'Entamoeba'. Give the full name, Entamoeba histolytica.
Writing Entamoeba coli, which is a harmless species.
steps.memory_tip: Histolytica means tissue-dissolving, and that is exactly what makes the ulcers.
steps.margin_note: Full binomial name first, then one line linking it to the symptoms.

insider_note: This is a symptom-to-name question, so both the disease name and the full binomial of the organism must appear; a half name loses the mark.
